title: Shaders in GLSL ES 3.00 through studio::shader, with no version line of their own
note: Write shaders as GLSL ES 3.00 bodies and load them with studio::shader: the runtime adds the version and precision lines.
intent: Every destination draws through GLSL ES 3.00 (WebGL2 in the browser, ANGLE on the desktop), so a shader written for desktop GL fails on all of them. Write the source without any version line and load it with studio::shader(vertex, fragment); the runtime puts the ES 3.00 header and precision in front (null keeps raylib's default stage). Use in/out, texture(), and raylib's own names: fragTexCoord, fragColor, texture0, colDiffuse and an out vec4 finalColor in the fragment stage; vertexPosition, vertexTexCoord, vertexColor and mvp in the vertex stage. Set uniforms with GetShaderLocation once and SetShaderValue each frame from simulation state, never from the clock.
port: A shader belongs to the facet that draws with it; assign it to that facet's model materials in reset, after the model is loaded.

evidence.note: studio::shader(vs, fs) takes GLSL ES 3.00 without a version line; the runtime adds it and precision highp float.
The shader header every destination gets: ANGLE and WebGL2 both speak GLSL ES 3.00.
